filename: Calibrating Geophysical Predictions under Constrained Probabilistic Distributions.pdf
title: Calibrating Geophysical Predictions under Constrained Probabilistic Distributions
parameterization_target: subgrid eddy potential vorticity / turbulent flux forcing
code_availability: All data associated with this manuscript, along with code necessary to process the data and generate the figures can be found at https://github.com/zwhou99/Distribution-Informed-Prediction.
testbed_rationale: Provides a reproducible benchmark for online-coupled subgrid turbulence modeling in pyqg and air-sea pCO2 reconstruction from sparse data, supported by open code and data on GitHub.
pain_points: Offline-to-online drift: surrogates trained on short-horizon MSE fail to preserve invariant measures and energy spectra during long-term rollout.
Extreme data sparsity and sampling bias: e.g., SOCAT observes less than 1% of the ocean surface.
Requirement of prior steady-state distributions: the KSD calibration framework assumes access to a target knowledge distribution which may not always be readily available.
Vanishing gradients and brittleness in existing physics-informed losses when data are sparse.
extraction_notes: The paper investigates post-hoc calibration of machine learning predictions (both offline reconstruction and online parameterization) using Kernelized Stein Discrepancy (KSD) and normalization against known or modeled marginal distributions.
